cls: Selective neuronal potassium channel opener (SNEPCO); centrally acting non-opioid analgesic
pharm: Non-opioid centrally acting analgesic / muscle relaxant
quick: 100 mg three to four times daily; max 600 mg/day (short term)
With or without food; swallow whole
Caution in severe impairment; reduce dose
summary: Flupirtine is a centrally acting non-opioid analgesic and muscle relaxant (selective neuronal potassium channel opener). It is NOT FDA-approved; it was marketed in parts of Europe but its use was severely restricted/withdrawn by the EMA (2018) because of the risk of serious, sometimes fatal hepatotoxicity. Where still available, use is limited to short-term (max 2 weeks) acute pain when other analgesics are contraindicated, with weekly LFT monitoring.
indications: Short-term treatment of acute pain in adults only when treatment with other analgesics (e.g., NSAIDs, weak opioids) is contraindicated (per restricted EMA/regional approval)
Note: NOT FDA-approved; EMA restricted/withdrew use due to hepatotoxicity

dosage.d: 100 mg three to four times daily; up to 200 mg up to four times (max 600 mg/day)
Start at lower end and reduce frequency

admin: Use only short-term (no more than 2 weeks) and only when other analgesics are contraindicated
Check liver function before starting and weekly during treatment
Stop immediately if LFTs rise or signs of liver injury appear
moa: Flupirtine is a selective neuronal potassium (Kv7/KCNQ, M-current) channel opener (SNEPCO). By stabilizing the resting membrane potential it indirectly inhibits NMDA receptor activation, reducing neuronal excitability and nociceptive transmission and producing analgesia and muscle-relaxant effects without opioid receptor activity.

absolute: Pre-existing hepatic disease or hepatic encephalopathy risk
Alcohol abuse / concomitant other potentially hepatotoxic drugs
Tinnitus (increased risk of hepatotoxicity per regional labeling)

preg: Avoid; not recommended in pregnancy due to insufficient safety data.
lact: Avoid; flupirtine passes into breast milk in small amounts. Discontinue nursing or the drug.
renal: Use with caution and reduce dose in renal impairment; avoid in severe impairment.
hepatic: Contraindicated in pre-existing hepatic disease and in patients with alcohol abuse. Hepatotoxicity (including fatal liver failure) is the key safety concern; stop immediately if liver enzymes rise.

major: Other hepatotoxic drugs (e.g., paracetamol/acetaminophen, carbamazepine) - increased liver injury risk; avoid combining
Warfarin/coumarins - flupirtine may potentiate anticoagulant effect; monitor INR
moderate: CNS depressants, alcohol, sedatives - additive sedation
Drugs highly bound to albumin (e.g., diazepam) - displacement interactions
interactions.food: May be taken with or without food.
interactions.alcohol: Avoid entirely; markedly increases hepatotoxicity risk.
interactions.diagnostics: May cause green discoloration of urine; can elevate liver transaminases; may cause false readings in some bilirubin/protein assays.

monitoring: Liver function tests before treatment and weekly during treatment
Signs/symptoms of liver injury (jaundice, dark urine, fatigue, anorexia)
Limit total treatment duration to 2 weeks
counsel: This medicine is only for short-term pain and must not be used longer than 2 weeks
You will need weekly blood tests for your liver
Stop and seek care if you notice yellow skin/eyes, dark urine, severe tiredness or loss of appetite
Do not drink alcohol while taking it
Your urine may turn green - this is harmless
pk: Store at room temperature, protect from light/moisture
pearls: NOT FDA-approved; EMA restricted then effectively withdrew it (2018) due to serious/fatal hepatotoxicity - sourcing is EMA/SmPC/BNF, not FDA
Use limited to short-term acute pain (<=2 weeks) only when other analgesics are contraindicated
Mandatory weekly liver function monitoring where still used
Harmless green discoloration of urine is common
Contraindicated with alcohol abuse, hepatic disease, myasthenia gravis and tinnitus
missed: Take the missed dose when remembered unless it is close to the next dose; then skip it. Do not double up. Because treatment is short-term, follow the prescriber's exact schedule.
overdose: Overdose may cause nausea, tachycardia, drowsiness, dry mouth, agitation/confusion and risk of hepatotoxicity. Treat symptomatically and supportively (gastric decontamination if early, forced diuresis, supportive care); monitor liver function. No specific antidote.
refs: SmPC / BNF national formulary information (non-FDA agent)
